query: For high-entropy-alloy protective coatings in wear-resistant applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their wear performance and why? Define a controlled change that would distinguish the hypothesis from a baseline, the directional observations expected if it is correct, the range over which it should hold, the prior evidence that supports it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Under dry sliding, the wear rate of Al-containing CrFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy (HEA) coatings is governed primarily by the in-situ formation of a continuous nanocrystalline Al2O3-rich tribo-oxide glaze; coatings that cannot form (or maintain) this glaze exhibit an order-of-magnitude higher wear.
generation.material_initial_state: Magnetron-sputtered CrFeCoNiAlx coatings (x = atomic ratio of Al to each base element) deposited to ~5 µm on hardened steel, fully dense, <200 nm grain size, identical residual stress and surface finish before testing.
generation.intervention: Increase Al content from x = 0.3 (baseline) to x = 1.3 while keeping total film thickness, microstructure and substrate constant.
generation.conditions: Room temperature, unlubricated ball-on-disk sliding against 6 mm Al2O3 counter-body, 5 N normal load, 0.1 m s⁻¹ sliding speed, 1000 m total sliding distance, ambient air (≈30 % RH).
generation.structural_mediator: A ~50–100 nm thick, adherent, fine-grained Al2O3 tribo-film that continuously covers the wear track during sliding.
generation.mechanism: Higher Al supply (>~25 at %) oxidizes preferentially, rapidly forming and replenishing a dense Al2O3 layer; this glaze reduces direct metal-to-metal contact, lowers adhesive junction growth and ploughing, and inhibits third-body abrasion, thereby cutting wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to x = 0.3, the x = 1.3 coating will show (a) ≥5× lower specific wear rate (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹), (b) ≥30 % lower steady-state coefficient of friction, and (c) a continuous Al2O3 film confirmed by TEM + EELS; the low-Al coating will show discontinuous, mixed Cr/Fe oxides and tribo-debris.
generation.baseline: CrFeCoNiAl0.3 coating tested under identical conditions; expected to form patchy, porous oxides and suffer high wear (10⁻⁴–10⁻³ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹).
generation.boundary: Effect should hold for 20 °C–400 °C dry sliding, normal loads 1–10 N, sliding speeds 0.05–0.2 m s⁻¹, and Al between ≈25–40 at %. Outside these, different oxides or melting may dominate.
generation.uncertainty: No direct quantitative data yet link Al2O3 film continuity with wear in this HEA system; other elements (Cr-spinel, NiO) or mechanical strengthening could co-dominate. Magnitude (5×) is an estimate.

falsification_experiment.design: Repeat the ball-on-disk test while stopping every 200 m to perform cross-sectional FIB-TEM on the wear track, mapping oxide chemistry and thickness for both Al levels.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, despite ≥1.3× higher Al content, (i) no continuous Al2O3-rich tribo-film (>80 % area coverage) forms and (ii) the wear rate is not at least 3× lower than the x=0.3 baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
